chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari told us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn Muslim or others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Marry, for indeed, I will compete with the nations tomorrow on the Day of Resurrection through you. Even the miscarried fetus will come as a muhabnati to the Gate of Paradise, and it will be said to him: Enter Paradise. He will say: No, until my parents enter before me.

key_terms.مُحْبَنَطِيًا: A specific posture or state of the fetus (often translated as coming with head down or in a specific manner)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of marriage in Shia hadith regarding the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar* underscores the spiritual merit of marriage by linking it to the Prophet's intercession and the expansion of the Muslim community (Ummah) on the Day of Resurrection. It further illustrates the profound familial bonds in the afterlife, where even a miscarried fetus (saqat) exhibits filial piety by waiting for its parents' entry into Paradise, reflecting the continuity of family ties beyond death.
